title: Sectionlab
summary: Build a cross-section from library shapes (solid, hollow, rolled or built-up I/H, channel, angle, tee, Z and cross sections, and cold-formed angles, channels, Zs and top hats, with a radius on any corner, holes and several materials) by dragging, and read its area, centroid, second moments, principal axes, section moduli, radii of gyration and first moments Q. A torsion constant is given only where a formula has been measured against a numerical Prandtl solution, with its accuracy, and a Ramberg–Osgood moment–curvature curve gives the moment at a strain limit, Z_p and the shape factor. Hand calculations work the closed-form properties step by step by composite parts (area, centroid, the parallel-axis theorem, principal axes, section moduli, radii of gyration and the torsion formula), every number the page's own, with Save Markdown and Copy Markdown. Exports a PDF report, PNGs, Markdown with the model as YAML that imports back, and a narrated Markdown deck (ending its results on the hand calculations, in the bf_emma voice) to open in beamdswitch for slides and a video. Results are checked against independent Python references; verify them independently.
